question: Does concurrent `hermit run --strict` scale past 150 cores? If it scales, the validate strategy inverts from serialize-to-avoid-contention to run-the-corpus-wide.
cpu: AMD EPYC 9D85 class, 158 physical cores x 2 SMT = 316 hardware threads

guest_variants.spin_guest_300m: ITERS=300000000, solo-free wall ~2.0s (used for the scaling sweep so makespan reflects compute not launch)

guest_determinism_check: spin_guest_30m emits acc=6007282469255529699 on every strict run; verified identical across all concurrent instances
harness: scratch/curve3-concurrent-hermit/sweep.sh (pinned variant) and inline free-instance loops
box_state: NOT quiet during measurement: hermit-231b curves 1+2 (cargo build / strict_compat) plus codex/rustc live. All rows labeled contended. High-N (>=128) knee NOT measured; requires a quiet box.

metrics.makespan_s: first launch to last exit, wall clock
metrics.agg_giter_per_s: N * guest_iters / makespan / 1e9 (absolute aggregate throughput, per owner: anchors not ratios)
metrics.per_instance_cpu_s: user+sys from /usr/bin/time for a single instance

reproduction: cc -O2 -DITERS=300000000ULL -o spin_guest_300m spin_guest.c; then for N in 1 2 4 8 16 32 64: launch N background `hermit run --strict -- spin_guest_300m` with NO taskset, measure first-launch-to-last-exit makespan and count nonzero exits. For the confinement contrast: compare `hermit run --strict` free vs under `taskset -c <core>`.
